- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -1.00) and model forecasts remain high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 1.00 for 3+ consecutive days) and model is flat or declining, increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots — cap forecast at +10% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If sentiment changes direction mid-period (e.g., from +1.00 to -0.33), reduce forecast by 5–15% to reflect mean reversion.  
- When news volume is low (≤1.0) and sentiment is volatile, model tends to overfit — apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility by 20–30%.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), adjust downward by 3–5% unless sentiment strongly supports upside.  
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is rising, reverse direction — model may be lagging sentiment reversal.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and model is trending, reduce forecast slope to avoid false momentum.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction unless sentiment is bullish and news volume is high.
